findings.evidence: “Does the user need to decide something here, or just be informed?” The following outcome table already supplies that decision; “Over-pasting a report nobody acts on buries the signal” is generic advice.
findings.fix: Keep the concrete rule about which outcomes get the full report and record the removal of the generic explanation.

findings.evidence: “Triggered by … passing document path(s)” matches unrelated file operations, and “needs review-and-fix” understates the supported review-only path.
findings.fix: Use when asked to review a design, specification, requirements document, RFC, or implementation plan before moving on, even if the user just asks whether it is ready to build. Dispatch a fresh-context reviewer, ground findings in the document’s worktree, and review at the document’s lifecycle stage. When revisions are authorized, route fixes through Superpowers, GSD, OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Kiro, BMAD, or the generic fixer and re-review up to the iteration cap. Supports /ai-kit-spec-review, --cross-ai, and --no-cross-ai. Not for writing a new spec, executing a plan, reviewing a code diff, or configuring reviewer lanes.

findings.evidence: The 580-line body includes a 65-line “Lane capability block, lenses and refusals” section with field inventories, refusal internals, and a separate owner-started edit operation.
findings.fix: Keep the dispatch decision, refusal handling, and rule against automatic post-approval edits in the body. Move the field inventories and diagnostic details to a top-level reference loaded when inspecting a lane, and the accept/reject procedure to a reference loaded only when the owner asks to run the edit-lens pass. Preserve all behavior and attribution.

findings.evidence: “Read this when a review keeps a round log,” but SKILL.md Step 1 needs this file’s fold-check command under --no-cross-ai, and Step 4 can need disagreement classification without a round log.
findings.fix: Gate the ping, switch, and partial-status sections on a round log; explicitly direct native-only runs to the fold-check and disagreement command sections when those steps apply.

findings.evidence: “Remove $RUN_TMP_DIR (rm -rf …) only when the Surface outcome is Approved” gates deletion on the outcome, not on whether the directory is owned by this run. A resumed invocation gets the path from a pointer rather than creating it itself.
findings.fix: Before recursive deletion, verify that the canonical path is an identified temp directory created for this review and matches its saved run metadata. If ownership or path confinement cannot be verified, keep it and report the path.

findings.evidence: Step 2 says “Any other text on the Status line” is Issues Found. The merge parser instead accepts any value starting with “approved.” A read-only check confirmed that “### Status: Approved pending clarification” renders as a clean “### Status: Approved” after merge.
findings.fix: Use the same closed approval vocabulary in native and merged paths: only the exact Approved and Approved (partial) statuses can approve. Regression-test an unknown status that begins with Approved.

findings.evidence: Step 0.6 says ARCHETYPE is “per-document,” but the native and subprocess templates supply one ARCHETYPE value and one FRAMEWORK_PROFILE_PATH for every path. A GSD context file and its plan have no defined way to carry different review ceilings in the same dispatch.
findings.fix: Pass an explicit path-to-archetypes-and-profile mapping in both templates, keep grounding-only inputs separate, and use the same mapping for fix routing and resume. Include a mixed context-and-plan example that never applies the plan checklist to context.

findings.evidence: The stage-gap output says “Reviewed <existing> as <archetype>,” although Step 0.6 says to stop and offer that review, and the input gate already stops on a nonexistent named path.
findings.fix: For a known lifecycle gap, say what exists and offer to review it without claiming it was reviewed. Keep the missing-path failure for an explicit nonexistent file, and define how a request naming only an artifact type reaches the stage check.

findings.evidence: The GSD handoff example says “Run: /gsd-plan-phase 2 --reviews (findings: EFFECTIVE_REPORT_PATH),” but the preceding branch hands off specifically when REVIEWS.md may be absent or stale, and says the planner ignores the trailing note. The upstream workflow uses /gsd:plan-phase and /gsd:review on its Claude command surface.
findings.fix: In the missing or stale REVIEWS.md branch, give the phase file’s exact path and ask the owner to put or approve the current report’s findings there before rerunning the planner. Resolve the command name from the installed GSD surface and link the dated upstream workflow for the --reviews prerequisite.

findings.evidence: “Claude Code’s one-shot jobs at those minutes can fire up to 90 s early” is a version-sensitive scheduling claim without a dated vendor source. Anthropic’s scheduled-tasks documentation confirms the jitter.
findings.fix: Cite https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks#when-a-one-shot-task-runs-early with the date checked, and retain the not-before check and the manual fallback when scheduling cannot be confirmed.

findings.evidence: The case expects config-status to report “active” and a finding to route to writing-plans, but the supplied live roster names fake/placeholder-model-1 and the case supplies no simulated inventory or reviewer report. Parts of the result depend on the host instead of the fixture.
findings.fix: Use an isolated fake runner with a deterministic model listing and a known blocking report for the routing cases; pin the temporary project root and the available or unavailable native handlers.

findings.evidence: “Runs no config-status and reads no config.toml under --no-cross-ai” conflates reviewer selection with the native lens lookup: the documented capability-block call scans skill roles through config_io.cfg_load_layers.
findings.fix: Assert that --no-cross-ai skips config-status, quota probing, sizing, ping, and cross-AI selection. Test native lens lookup separately, and add a review-only findings case that asserts no fixer or native rewrite runs without consent.
